summary: This note surveys the main trade policy levers countries use to improve international competitiveness, including trade facilitation, innovation, infrastructure, tariffs and non-tariff measures, trade agreements, human capital, domestic policy coherence, sustainability, digital trade and responses to trade wars. Each theme is tied to a dated event or expert statement between September 2023 and February 2024. It closes with an outlook pointing to the International Trade Summit scheduled for March 10, 2024.
one_line: Overview of trade policy tools for international competitiveness, from facilitation and infrastructure to digital trade, with 2023-2024 events and expert views.
key_facts: Trade facilitation means the simplification, modernization, and harmonization of export and import processes.

At the World Economic Forum summit on October 8, 2023, Trade Minister Liam Robertson said reducing trade barriers could enhance competitiveness by lowering transaction costs and boosting trade volumes.
On September 12, 2023, the Global Trade Conference unveiled initiatives to shift resources toward research and development (R&D).
On September 15, 2023, a panel including infrastructure expert Dr. Helen Zhou detailed plans for a billion-dollar upgrade to the country's freight corridor.

On September 25, 2023, a National Trade Council report chaired by Tom Henderson recommended carefully designed tariffs and non-tariff measures (NTMs) to protect local industries while encouraging competitiveness.
At the Trade Leaders' Forum on December 12, 2023, Secretary Annabelle Rodriguez cited trade agreements as opening new markets, reducing export costs, and providing legal certainty.
On January 5, 2024, the Department of Labor and Education announced a partnership to launch vocational training programs for export-oriented sectors.
The Federal Economic Summit of February 9, 2024, showcased domestic policy coherence as instrumental in propelling the economy.
At the Green Economy Conference on October 22, 2023, Dr. Rachel Kim said eco-friendly trade policies can preserve the environment and open markets for green technology and services.
The Digital Trade Symposium on November 28, 2023, showcased strategies including cybersecurity investment and digital payment systems for cross-border transactions.
In a January 18, 2024 press release, Trade Minister Liam Robertson highlighted realtime adjustments to trade policies as key amid trade wars and geopolitical uncertainty.
The next International Trade Summit is scheduled for March 10, 2024.
